title: Original pesticide and veterinary source concordance

ctr2018.commencement: On publication in the Official Gazette; not the January 2019 upload filename.

method.comparison: Ordered one-to-one core-row comparison, retaining all original cells, compound-cell expansion, headings, symbols and page references. Numeric equality is not legal scope approval.
method.tableExtraction: pdfplumber table cells; 14 compound pesticide cells expand to 42 normalized entries. Page 25 Praziquantel pig row is manually recovered from the rendered source because its open top border defeats grid extraction.
method.visualReview: Selected commencement, qualifier, name-variant, repeated-row, milk-unit and direction pages were rendered and inspected. All table entries were compared from extracted cells; not every page was manually inspected.
method.inheritedHeading: Veterinary originalPrecedingHeading records physical layout only. It does not overrule explicit food text, the Oxytetracycline override, or either source-locked repeated Muscle row.

findings.title: Two duplicate pesticide article pairs remain held
findings.detail: The original page 33 itself prints Carbaryl/Maize at 0.02 within the food-grains cell and 0.5 separately. It prints Carbendazim/Rice at 2.0 within the food-grains cell and 2* separately. Equal numeric values do not erase the latter LOQ marker. No preferred row is selected.

findings.title: Food-grain scope differs from the stored label
findings.detail: At serial 36, page 34 prints Wheat 0.5, Rice 0.5 and Food grains 0.05. The stored Other food grains label adds a qualification absent from the original. That normalized row is held pending legal article reconciliation; wheat and rice values are not reassigned.

findings.title: Alpha Cypermethrin needs its own identity check
findings.detail: Serial 50 page 36 gives Cypermethrin cottonseed oil 0.01 and sub-entry (a) Alpha Cypermethrin cotton seed oil 0.05. Matching the spacing of a food label must not choose the higher value. The sub-entry requires verified Alpha Cypermethrin identity. Serial 5 also separately prints Alpha cypermethrin 0.05.

findings.title: Five chemical-name differences require reconciliation
findings.detail: Serials 7, 37, 46, 55 and 142 differ between original and stored names, affecting 24 rows. The evidence retains both spellings and the full metabolite wording; no authoritative chemical alias or correction is inferred.

findings.title: Two repeated Muscle rows remain source-locked
findings.detail: Original page 19 repeats Muscle at the end of Amoxicillin after the Sheep block and after the Cattle block of the tetracycline group. No new species heading identifies those repetitions. The original layout does not justify inventing a missing species or dropping the duplicate.

findings.title: Milk units and the narrowed fish drug label are retained
findings.detail: Ceftiofur, Gentamicin and Spectinomycin cattle-milk limits expressly use mg/l. Serial 7 fish is labelled Oxytetracycline in the drug column, not the entire three-drug heading. Pre-December overlap with the separate seafood clause remains held.

findings.title: Honey and prohibited-use thresholds do not authorize treatment
findings.detail: The 12 honey rows match original page 18, including the two collective-group conditions. The 14 prohibited classes and their 0.001 mg/kg EMRL, with 0.0003 mg/kg for chloramphenicol, match pages 17–18. These are not permission to administer antibiotics.

findings.title: Pesticide defaults remain conditional on the applicable direction
findings.detail: The 11 January 2021 clarification addresses the 213-table/default scope for agricultural commodities and physically processed foods. The 8 April 2024 spice/herb order supersedes both 2022 orders and has specific FSSAI/Codex/registration branches. Neither becomes a blanket processed-food exemption or automatic 0.01/0.1 mg/kg rule.

reviewBoundary.scope: Original 2018 pesticide and 2024 veterinary/honey/prohibited-use texts only, with the two specified pesticide directions. This is not every NOTS amendment, method, packaging, labelling, claims or legal interpretation.
